The Future with Going to - Information Questions
The future with going to in interrogative form can also be used with information questions.
What are you going to explain?
Where is the presentation going to take place this time?

We can create questions in the future with going to to ask for specific information on someone or something.

To do this, we can follow one of these structures depending on the kind of information we are trying to get:

Wh word + verb to be + subject + going to + complement


Example: Who is going to help me with the presentation?

Wh word + object + verb to be + subject + going to + complement


Example: What class name are you going to use to start that object?

In the table below, you will find every wh word you can use to ask for information with the explained structure.

Static Members of a C# Class
We define class as static using the static keyword.

The keyword static implies there is only one copy of the static member. Static variables are used for defining constants because their values can be taken out by invoking the class without creating an instance of it. It can be initialized outside the member function and outside or inside the class definition.

Johnson: Hello, Lisa. Congratulations on your course! Everyone loved it!
Lisa: Thank you, Sir. I'm very pleased, although I have to admit I was a bundle of nerves before the course took place.
Johnson: Let's talk about your next course. What are you going to explain?
Lisa: I believe the students need to learn the concept of "classes." They need to know how to define a blueprint for a data type. By defining this, they will know what an object of the class consists of and the operations that can be performed on that object.

Johnson: I see! What are you going to say about syntax?
Lisa: I am going to write and explain the syntax. I will write the keyword plus the class name and then the class body enclosed by curly braces. Access specifies the access rules for the members and the class itself. When not mentioned, the default access specifier for a class type is internal.
Johnson: Great skills, Lisa! What else are you going to include in the presentation?
Lisa: Class constructor and destructor.
Johnson: Why are you going to include these two topics?
Lisa: Because a class constructor has exactly the same name as that of the class and doesn't have a return type. It is an essential function of a class that is executed whenever we create a new object of that class. On the other hand, a destructor is executed whenever an object of its class goes out of scope; it has the same name of the class and the prefixed tilde.

Johnson: Are you adding anything else?
Lisa: The other topic will be the static member. Do you want me to talk about anything in special?
Johnson: I think these three topics will be enough.
Lisa: Where is the presentation going to take place this time?
Johnson: I don't have that information yet.
Lisa: I heard I'm not going to be the only presenter. Who will be on the platform with me?
Johnson: I suppose it will be Alison. Be prepared; the presentation is on Tuesday morning.
